originality.rationale: The original contribution is only the complete hyperflex-refined joint proper/hyperflex F3 spectrum plus the unique maximum orbit and its contact geometry. Bergvall 2022 quantitatively counts Frobenius classes for degree-two del Pezzo surfaces, likely already implying the unrefined F3 rational-bitangent distribution: that weaker statement is expressly excluded from originality. The geometry of individual line-contact divisors is not a consequence of a Frobenius 28-bitangent permutation alone.
residual_risks: The 2022 Bergvall Frobenius-class classification may be further combined with an existing hyperflex-locus stratification to derive part or all of the table; no such fully worked table was identified in the material inspected.
Earlier unindexed or unpublished exhaustive finite-field computations might already contain the same contact-refined counts.
No literature search establishes absolute priority or global uniqueness; independent external review has not been performed.

value.rationale: Refining Frobenius-fixed odd theta characteristics into proper contact divisors versus quadruple-contact hyperflexes measures a natural genus-three Weierstrass phenomenon not recoverable from bitangent counts alone. The complete joint distribution and unique 312-equation maximizer projective orbit distinguish genuine geometric configurations at the same arithmetic bitangent frequency.
